findings.claim: UTF-8 recovery uses an offset relative to the BOM-stripped input to slice the original bytes. It can drop the preceding complete record, suppress money in at the limit and attribute the UTF-8 error to the wrong line.
findings.repro: Use a BOM-prefixed Monzo CSV with the header Transaction ID,Date,Type,Name,Amount,Currency,Balance. Put tx_1,01/01/2026,Faster payment,ACME,9999999999999.99,GBP,1.00 on line 2 and the same values with tx_2 and 02/01/2026 on line 3. Terminate both rows with LF and start line 4 with byte 0xFF. Run cma import monzo. The recovery slice cuts the last two balance digits and newline from line 3 and then drops that row. It reports line 3 and omits that money in reached the limit. The runner’s CR-only and multiline UTF-8 tests use files without a BOM.

findings.claim: The Monzo CLI interpolates the import error into Rich markup. A closing tag in a rejected cell can raise a markup error and suppress both the record-start line and the flow-limit diagnostic.
findings.repro: Use a Monzo CSV with the header Transaction ID,Date,Type,Name,Amount,Currency,Balance. Put tx_1,01/01/2026,Faster payment,ACME,9999999999999.99,GBP,1.00 on line 2 and tx_2,02/01/2026,Faster payment,ACME,0.01,GBP,[/red] on line 3. Run cma import monzo. The converter includes both the money-in limit and the invalid Balance on line 3 in MonzoImportError. Rich interprets the cell’s unmatched closing tag while rendering that error.
